escalate.headline: This test shows a noticeable change.
questions_to_ask_your_doctor: What follow-up test or scan do you recommend to check this result?
Could another health issue or medicine cause this change?
What symptoms or changes should I look out for right now?
escalate.recommended_action: Contact your clinic to schedule a review and follow-up scan.
escalate.what_this_means: This blood test is higher than your usual personal range. A rise can happen for different health reasons. Your cancer care team will check your results and talk with you about next steps.

explained.headline: This test result looks stable.
questions_to_ask_your_doctor: Does my routine monitoring schedule stay the same?
Are there any new symptoms I should report before my next visit?
When is my next scheduled blood test or clinic appointment?
explained.what_this_means: Small day-to-day changes in your body are normal and expected. This result stays within the expected range for your routine surveillance. Your oncology team will continue your regular monitoring plan.

needs_repeat.headline: This result needs a quick repeat test.
questions_to_ask_your_doctor: When and where should I repeat this blood test?
Are there any special instructions before my next blood draw?
What specific symptoms should I watch for while waiting for the repeat test?
needs_repeat.recommended_action: Repeat blood test within 7 to 14 days at your local laboratory.
needs_repeat.verbal_band: Analytical uncertainty (suspected lab or specimen variation)
needs_repeat.what_this_means: A sudden shift in a lab number often comes from lab equipment variation rather than a true change in your body. A single high result is not a diagnosis. Repeating the blood test gives your doctor an accurate and reliable picture.

false_alarm_explained.clinical_context: Patient on surveillance. CA 15-3 increases from 20 to 23 U/mL (1.15x), below RCV threshold.
false_alarm_explained.narrative: The calculated probability of true progression is 1%. The calculated probability of analytical or pre-analytical error is 0%. The calculated probability of baseline biological stability is 98%. The biological reference change value threshold is 31%. The observed marker ratio is 1.15 relative to baseline. The recommended clinical action is explained.
false_alarm_explained.title: Benign Fluctuation: Biological Noise Within RCV Adjudicated as Explained

j2_surprising_repeat.clinical_context: Patient on surveillance with stable CA 15-3 (~18 U/mL). Day 360 shows sudden jump to 180 U/mL.
j2_surprising_repeat.narrative: The calculated probability of true progression is 0%. The calculated probability of analytical or pre-analytical error is 100%. The calculated probability of baseline biological stability is 0%. The biological reference change value threshold is 31%. The observed marker ratio is 10.00 relative to baseline. The recommended clinical action is needs_repeat.
j2_surprising_repeat.title: Journey J2: Surprising Marker Spike (Analytical Error) Adjudicated to Repeat

real_progression_escalate.clinical_context: Patient on surveillance. CA 15-3 surges from 15 to 37.8 U/mL (2.5x), exceeding RCV.
real_progression_escalate.narrative: The calculated probability of true progression is 99%. The calculated probability of analytical or pre-analytical error is 1%. The calculated probability of baseline biological stability is 0%. The biological reference change value threshold is 31%. The observed marker ratio is 2.50 relative to baseline. The recommended clinical action is escalate.
real_progression_escalate.title: True Recurrence: Biomarker Elevation Exceeding RCV Adjudicated to Escalate
